$comment: Scoop manifest for zoorikctl, rendered per release by cli/zoorikctl/packaging/render.sh and
SCOOP IS THE WINDOWS PACKAGE MANAGER THIS SHIPS WITH FIRST, and the reason is that it is
the only one of the three that can ship at all without somebody else's approval. A Scoop
bucket is a git repository of JSON files: publishing is a push, updating is a push, and a
customer installs with `scoop bucket add storagetax https://github.com/storagetax/scoop-bucket`
then `scoop install zoorikctl`. No account, no review queue, no publisher identity.
winget is the one a Windows engineer reaches for first and is a named blocker: every
version is a pull request into microsoft/winget-pkgs that a human reviews, and the
manifest requires a stable publisher identity. It is worth doing and it cannot be done
Chocolatey is a second account plus a moderation queue, and its audience overlaps winget
almost entirely. It is not planned unless a customer asks.
